category_definitions.known_in_silence_but_different_outcome: the target was still known in silence but the task ended differently — the uplink changed the outcome
category_definitions.load_bearing_outcome_only_with_uplink: never known at all in silence — the report was necessary for the task to exist for any robot
category_definitions.redundant_knowledge_and_outcome: some robot knew this target with no uplink at a step no later than with it, and the task ended the same way — the emission carried nothing
category_definitions.uplink_bought_time_same_outcome: known without the uplink too, but later; the outcome happened to survive the delay

redundancy_against_the_silence_counterfa.method: paired by seed, target by target: arm A1 (immediate, lossless) against arm A2 (always_hold). A2 is the only archived deployed-path run where the uplink sent nothing, so it is the counterfactual the archive actually supports.

savings_ceiling.note: strict = only emissions redundant in both knowledge and outcome; permissive additionally counts emissions where silence delayed knowledge but the recorded outcome survived. The permissive figure is NOT a savings estimate: A2's robots moved on a different trajectory precisely because they were not told, so 'later but still on time' is not a stable counterfactual. Only the strict figure may be quoted, and only as a ceiling on what a controller could aim at.

what_is_not_on_disk.budgeted_deployed_path: no archived run combines an enforced --comm-budget-bytes with the deployed information path (gossip_interval=2, comm_range=0.3). Round 16 is deployed but never binding (budget_refused_sends == 0 everywhere); rounds 12/15 are budgeted but isolated.
what_is_not_on_disk.interior_cost_points: the deployed archive holds two cost points only: 0 B (A2) and 14 573.3 B (A1). A cost-minimising controller needs the interior, and the interior cannot be obtained offline because silencing a report changes which robot is in line of sight later, which is what the unbilled channel depends on.
what_is_not_on_disk.recipient_heterogeneity: subscribers is a single scalar for the whole step (integrated_sar/comm_policy.py:112); per-recipient pricing does not exist, so 'address fewer robots' is not an available lever (round 17: global_fanout_is_only_a_scalar).
what_is_not_on_disk.the_two_free_channels_separately: the line-of-sight truth refresh and the one-hop gossip live in the same function (old_task_env.py:477-512) behind the same interval gate (:1107-1110), and every archived arm either leaves both on or switches both off. Which of the two carries the redundant knowledge is therefore not answerable from the archive, and the savings a controller could chase cannot be attributed to one channel.
